title: Database indexes in 60 seconds
caption: Database indexes in 60 seconds: why one line of SQL can make a slow query thousands of times faster. #database #sql #backend

scenes.title: Indexes
scenes.say: Same query, same data. One takes a minute, the other a millisecond.
Find one email in ten million rows, with no index, and the database checks every single row.
An index is like the index at the back of a book.

items.title: Sorted
items.say: It keeps a column's values in sorted order.

items.title: Pointers
items.say: Each one points to its row.

items.title: Tree
items.text: a few hops to any value
items.say: Stored as a tree, so any value is a few hops away.

scenes.say: One line, and the lookup goes from scanning everything to a handful of steps.
The catch: every insert also updates the index. That's an index. Faster reads, slightly slower writes.
